page_017__left__b002.text:
The total difficulty of
a route consists of the
fixed-rope-route dif-
ficulty, the rock climbing
difficulty (if there are un-
secured sections) and the
demand of the route. An
alpine route at 3000 me-
ters with a long approach
and descent and an ele-
vation gain of 1000m is
much more difficult than
an E grades sport climb
(i.e. Casto Ferrata Park)
in the valley.

page_017__left__b007.text:
English Version
Grade of difficulty
ope securing at exposed
sections and some very
short ladders. Only inex-
perienced mountaineers
need fixed rope equipment
for self-securing.
B (moderate): Stee-
per rock sections with
ropes, aglets und tricky
bridges. Also experienced
climbers start to belay
themselves. An additional
rope for kids and absolute
beginners is needed.
C (difficult): Verti-
cal rock sections, even
some small overhangs.
Less aglets and cramps.
Bridges require more arm

page_018__left__b004.text:
1: Hands needed to go up.
For beginners rope belay
required.
2: Rock climbing starts.
Everybody is belaying.
3: Vertical exposed rock.
Hooks for additional pro-
tection needed.

page_018__left__b009.text:
Beside the technical dif-
ficulties (A-G and clim-
bing grades) this grade
(1-3) shows the total
seriousness of the climb,
consisting of the route
length, alpine surround-
ing (snow, ice, exposure
and altitude), orientation
and missing emergency
exits.
